questions.a: No. Many members start with one intro programming course. If you can write a loop and an if-statement, you're ready for our beginner sessions.

C++, Python and Java. These are the languages ICPC allows, and the ones Kattis and Codeforces support best. Most competitive programmers end up using C++ for speed, but Python is a great place to start.
No. The club is free to join, and every platform we use (Kattis, Codeforces, CSES) is free.

questions.q: Do I have to be a Computer Science student?
questions.a: No. Any UWindsor student is welcome: engineering, math, science, business, anyone. To compete at ICPC you must meet ICPC's eligibility rules, and we'll help you check.

questions.q: How do I get on an ICPC team?
questions.a: Come to practice and club contests. Before the regional we help members form teams of three based on interest and skill, and we hold training sessions in the weeks before.

questions.q: I can't make every session. Is that okay?
questions.a: Yes. Come when you can. Problems and solutions from each session are posted on Discord so you can catch up.
